extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / citizens interested in current events and federal legislation
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting and statutory text excerpt describing the Burke-Wadsworth selective-service (peacetime conscription) bill: who must register, classification and selection procedures, exemptions, training/benefits, and related authorities. Intended to inform the public about the draft law's provisions and implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must register
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided in this act, it shall be the duty of every male citizen of the United States, and of every male alien residing in the United States, who, on the day or days fixed for the first or any subsequent registration, is between the ages of twenty-one and thirty-six, to present himself for and submit to registration at such time or places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration occurs on a day fixed by the President; summary news passages sometimes cited ages 21–35 but the statute text gives 21–36.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for training and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Every male citizen and male alien residing who is between the ages of twenty-one and thirty-six at the time fixed for registration shall be liable for training and service in the land or naval forces of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President is authorized to select and induct into the forces, from those registered and classified but not deferred or exempted, such number as required in the national interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical and mental fitness determination
rubrics_metrics.description: No man shall be inducted for training and service under this act unless and until he is acceptable to the land or naval forces for such training and service and his physical and mental fitness for such training and service has been satisfactorily determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local boards will have medical examiners and deputy examiners to assess fitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training period (length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each man inducted under the provisions shall serve for a training and service period of twelve consecutive months, unless sooner discharged; whenever the Congress has declared the national interest imperiled the twelve-month period may be extended by the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a baseline one-year training/service term with presidential extension authority in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-training reserve transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Each man, after completion of his period of training and service, shall be transferred to a reserve component of the land or naval forces and until he attains age forty-five, or until ten years after such transfer, or until discharge, shall be deemed a member of such reserve and subject to additional training/service as prescribed by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are provisions for relief from reserve liability for certain additional service in regular Army or National Guard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay and benefits parity
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to men inducted for training and service there shall be paid, allowed and extended the same pay, allowances, pensions, disability and death compensation and other benefits as are provided by law in the case of other enlisted men of like grades and length of service of that component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News summary specified trainees would receive $21 monthly for first four months and $30 subsequently (with opportunity for raises); statutory text mandates parity with like enlisted men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic employment limits for land forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons inducted into the land forces of the United States under this act shall not be employed beyond the limits of the territories and possessions of the United States, including the Philippine Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News summaries elsewhere in the article stated trainees could be used in the Western Hemisphere and U.S. possessions; the statute text limits land forces to U.S. territories and possessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum number inducted per year
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in time of war, not more than nine hundred thousand men shall be inducted for training and service under the provisions of this act in any one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill places a 900,000 limit on the number of trainees in the Army in any one year; news pieces gave estimates of initial call sizes (e.g., ~75,000 in November).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and quotas (impartiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of men for training and service shall be made in an impartial manner, under such rules and regulations as the President may prescribe... Quotas of men to be inducted shall be determined for each state, territory and the District of Columbia, and for subdivisions thereof, on the basis of the actual number of men liable for such training and service but who are not deferred after classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law requires no discrimination on account of race or color; quotas may be based on estimates and later adjusted, and credits are given for residents already in the forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration procedure at local level
rubrics_metrics.description: On a day set by the President, the men will register at their voting precincts; registrars forward registration cards to county clerks who distribute them to local boards. Each board will shuffle cards, give serial numbers which are sent to Washington where a lottery determines selection order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some 700,000 regular election officials will assist; local boards will be apportioned credits against quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local boards structure and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be about 6,500 local boards of four or five citizens each, appointed by the President and serving without pay; each board will have a medical examiner and perhaps several deputy examiners, and will be assisted by advisory groups of doctors, lawyers, businessmen, farmers, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State headquarters staffs will be created and each governor will nominate a state director; national committee will report totals to Washington.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionnaire and classification information
rubrics_metrics.description: The questionnaire distributed after registration will be lengthy—more than one hundred questions—divided into thirteen series covering general subjects (e.g., physical condition, dependency, religious conviction, occupation, citizenship, claim/waiver for deferment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions cover personal and dependent information, court records, and such; not all questions apply to every registrant; answers will be kept confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferments and exemptions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferment of training would be granted men with dependents and some other special classes (including ministers, theological students, men in essential occupations, certain government officers, aliens, the physically unfit and conscientious objectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferments criteria are handled during classification by local boards; supporting affidavits required for dependents; categories like 'important to defense' occupations may be deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific service exemptions (prior service)
rubrics_metrics.description: In time of peace, persons such as those who have satisfactorily served at least three consecutive years in the Regular Army, or certain combinations of National Guard and Regular Army service meeting prescribed durations, shall be relieved from liability to serve in any reserve component and from training/service under Section 3(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute lists multiple prior-service scenarios that confer exemption from new obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscientious objector handling and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Those claiming religious conviction against war who have well‑founded records as conscientious objectors, if sustained by the local board, shall be assigned to noncombatant service; if not sustained, the claimant is entitled to appeal to the appeal board, which shall refer the matter to the Department of Justice for inquiry and hearing; after hearing the Department shall recommend to the appeal board appropriate disposition (noncombatant assignment or civilian work of national importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal process includes administrative hearings and notification; final appeal to the President can be had in rare cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal information and that on dependents, court records, and such will be kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration cards record vital statistics; the questionnaire must be returned in a short time (five days in summaries) and will be used for classification purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to return to employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of training, a conscripted man would be entitled to return to his former job—unless changed circumstances made it impossible for his employer to rehire him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law contemplates job-protection tendencies but recognizes practical limits if employer cannot rehire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting rights while in service
rubrics_metrics.description: The men in service would be entitled to vote, providing their States of residence had absentee voting laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainees' enfranchisement depends on state absentee-voting provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No call without appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: No men could be called to service until Congress made appropriations for their training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President's authority to call men into training is therefore conditioned on Congressional funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial plant takeover authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The final version included provision for the President to take over industrial plants, on a rental basis, when necessary to get defense orders filled expeditiously; the owner would receive rent and fair and just compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manufacturer declined to give the Government preference or refused to fill a defense order, the Government could step in and operate the plant; refusal could bring penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for refusing defense orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The manufacturer would be subject to maximum penalties of three years' imprisonment and $500,000 fine if he declined to give the Government preference on a defense order or refused to fill it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute contemplates criminal penalties for obstruction of defense production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection credits and quota adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotas shall be determined on the basis of actual numbers of men liable but not deferred after classification; credits shall be given for residents already in the land and naval forces; until actual numbers are known quotas may be based on estimates and subsequent adjustments shall be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computations will follow rules and regulations prescribed by the President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of training facilities before induction
rubrics_metrics.description: No man shall be inducted for such training and service until adequate provision shall have been made for such shelter, sanitary facilities, water supplies, heating and lighting arrangements, medical care and hospital accommodations for such men, as may be determined by the Secretary of War or the Secretary of the Navy to be essential to public and personal health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Induction is conditional on logistical readiness as determined by executive branch secretaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer induction opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the limits of the quota for a subdivision, any person between the ages specified shall be afforded an opportunity to volunteer for induction into the land or naval forces for training and service; but no man who so volunteers shall be inducted so long as he is deferred after classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteering does not override classification-based deferments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification procedure and required support for claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Each man will be entitled to state his claim for deferment, if any, to be passed on; supporting affidavits will be required of those claimed as dependents and of the man's employer or business associates; no man's answers will be taken for granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local boards will require documentation to substantiate deferment claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative structure for national organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A national headquarters will be established in Washington reporting state totals; a national committee with civilians and trained military officers will form the administrative nucleus; Governors nominate state directors and staffs for state headquarters which in turn create local boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This large administrative apparatus (state directors, local boards, advisory groups) is intended to manage registration, classification, and induction across the country.
